items.title: Petrol stations tried to 'shape' the market – now it's shaping them
items.description: Petrol stations in our biggest cities hiked prices ahead of global oil prices, but experts say their profit margins are now much slimmer.

items.title: Worst-case government modelling shows how long fuel stockpile lasts if imports slow
items.description: Diesel stocks would last about six months if Australia's imports dropped by 20 per cent, according to modelling compiled for the federal government early in the Middle East war.

items.title: Insiders profit as pressure points mount on global economy
items.description: Global stock markets, which for the past month have been remarkably restrained as the Middle East crisis unfolded, have begun to wobble.

items.title: Live: Wong reiterates Australia will not provide boots on ground in Iran war
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong says Australia has been clear that it will not provide troops on the ground for an operation against Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Israel backs down over holy site, Pope rebukes Hegseth, and what else you should know
items.description: Donald Trump renews threats against Iran's energy infrastructure while his secretary of war faces an apparent rebuke from the pope.

items.title: Trump threatens to 'obliterate' Kharg Island if Iran refuses deal to end war
items.description: As thousands more US troops arrive in the Middle East, Donald Trump threatens to wipe out Iran's energy plants and oil wells if it does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Iran's 'safe passage' signals a new global divide
items.description: China is now the world's largest crude oil importer, and Iran — though a discounted and often opaque supplier — remains a consistent part of that supply mix.

items.title: From Porepunkah to Thologolong: The long search for Dezi Freeman
items.description: When the parents of Senior Constable Vadim de Waart-Hottart flew to Melbourne for a police service, little did they know their son's killer would emerge just days later.

items.title: How one man's stolen identity was used to run a cult
items.description: In mid-2009 British citizen Simon Kadwill-Kelly was catching a ferry returning from France. Within minutes of trying to board he found out his identity had been stolen.

items.title: Transphobia nearly killed Kaz. Now he just wants to be 'me'
items.description: This WA teenager was depressed, ill, and missing out on school. He says it was part of the toll transphobia took on him.

items.title: Vaping likely to cause cancer, new Australian review of evidence finds
items.description: Nicotine-based vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancer, according to a new review of evidence. Experts say there needs to be tougher enforcement of vape laws in Australia.

items.title: How supermarket chicken could get cheaper because of grain breakthrough
items.description: Australian researchers develop a high-protein sorghum variety, hoping to replace expensive feed grains in livestock systems that could mean cheaper meat and eggs.

items.title: Live: Wall Street mixed as Australian consumers await two big decisions
items.description: Wall Street was mixed overnight as Australian consumers await two big decisions. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Five social media companies investigated over response to teen ban
items.description: Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube are being investigated for potential noncompliance with the ban, almost four months after the laws came into force.

items.title: What happens if your house is underinsured?
items.description: If your home is underinsured, it means your insurance policy won't fully cover the cost of rebuilding, repairing or replacing it.

items.title: Will you fly high or fail to launch on our moon quiz?
items.description: As NASA gets ready to launch humans around the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years, buckle up and let's see if your space knowledge is up to our quiz.

items.title: This luminous film shows a side of Iraq many Westerners have never seen
items.description: Filmmaker Hasan Hadi had to bring flowers to school to celebrate Saddam Hussein’s birthday. That memory loosely informs his beautiful debut feature, The President’s Cake.

items.title: Draft report into ANU's controversial cuts critical of university's council
items.description: ANU's council approved a massive $250 million cost-cutting program without clear evidence it was needed or achievable, according to an assessment in a draft audit office report.

items.title: Passengers fear further V/Line overcrowding as free travel begins
items.description: Commuters say they are worried overcrowding on V/Line train services could worsen as free travel begins for Victorians to ease the pain of the fuel crisis.

items.title: Businesses report increase in abuse from customers as fuel crisis worsens
items.description: From pile-on comments on social media to roadside slurs, local businesses are reminding their communities to "be kind to the little guy" amid the fuel crisis.

items.title: 'A succulent Chinese meal?': These are the 2026 Sounds of Australia
items.description: A variety of iconic Australian recordings are added to the Sounds of Australia collection, as part of an annual update by the National Film and Sound Archive.

items.title: NT paramedics face record assault rates, critical resourcing shortages
items.description: The ABC rode-along with St John Ambulance NT paramedics to hear the impact under-resourcing is having on the workforce, including stories of staff being assaulted on the job.

items.title: 'You are just an immigrant': Millions in unpaid wages, modern slavery uncovered
items.description: Millions in stolen wages, threats of visa cancellation and modern slavery by Australian employers have been uncovered in the first year of a national program.

items.title: Safety officers to patrol Hobart CBD to curb antisocial behaviour
items.description: A trio of council-employed public safety monitors will soon be patrolling "hot spots" in the Hobart CBD, to try to curb antisocial behaviour and theft.

items.title: Myanmar's military chief makes move to become next president
items.description: Myanmar's military chief has stepped down to seek the presidency in the general's latest efforts to maintain power behind the facade of a civilian administration.
